Unofficial until approved by the
  Alhambra City Council

  MINUTES
  Regular Meeting
  ALHAMBRA CITY COUNCIL
  Council Chambers, 111 South First Street
  April 22, 2024
  6:00 p.m.

ROLL CALL: At 6:07 p.m., on Monday, April 22, 2024, the Alhambra City Council met in the Council
Chambers of Alhambra City Hall.

PRESENT:  LEE, MALONEY, PÉREZ, ANDRADE-STADLER, MAZA
ABSENT:  NONE

Officials Present: City Manager Binnquist, Assistant City Manager Garcia, Deputy City Manager
Stover, City Attorney Montes, Assistant City Clerk Lamb McCarthy, Director of Parks & Recreation
Macias, Director of Library Services LohGuan, Director of Public Works/Utilities Ray, Director of
Finance Lieu, Director of Human Resources Ko, Director of Community Development Ho, Fire Chief
Ragusa, Revenue Supervisor Yu, Assistant Finance Director Tran, Assistant Police Chief Seki

FLAG SALUTE:  Led by Mayor Maza

LAND ACKNOWLEDGEMENT: We acknowledge that the land on which we are gathered is the
traditional, ancestral, and unceded territory of the Gabrielino/Tongva peoples. We seek to prioritize
respect for the historic culture and contemporary presence of the native peoples throughout California,
especially in the greater Los Angeles/Alhambra area. We come with respect and gratitude for the
Gabrielino/Tongva people who still consider themselves the caretakers of this land. It is through their
examples that we are reminded of our greater responsibility to take care of Mother Earth and to take
care of each other.

CEREMONIALS

1.  PROCLAMATIONS – F2M24-3
  A.  The Alhambra City Councill ratified the action of Mayor Maza in proclaiming April 26, 2024
  as ARBOR DAY in Alhambra. Mayor Maza presentrf the Arbor Day proclamation to Director
  of Parks & Recreation Michael Macias.
  B.  The Alhambra City Councill ratified the action of Mayor Maza in proclaiming the month of
  April, 2024 as OLDER AMERICANS MONTH in Alhambra. Mayor Maza presented the
  Older Americans Month proclamation to Director of Parks & Recreation Michael Macias.

2.  COMMENDATIONS: OUTGOING COMMISSION MEMBERS – F2M24-3, F2M24-37

  The City Council, on behalf of the citizens of Alhambra, wished to recognize the City’s outgoing
  Board and Commission members for their outstanding and dedicated service to the City of
  Alhambra. Mayor Maza presented the Certificates of Service.

  LEE LEIBERG
  Civil Service Commission/Board of Appeals
  (8 years)

4-22-24  1
   MAURICE NORRINGTON
  Parks & Recreation Commission
  (8 years)

  KIM LUU
  Environmental Sustainability Commission
  (8 years)

  DONALD MUMFORD
  Parks & Recreation Commission
  (8 years)

  ANTHONY SETO
  Parks & Recreation Commission
  (7 years)

  Mr. SETO and Mr. NORRINGTON were present to accept their certificates and thanked
  Council for the opportunity to serve on the Parks & Recreation Commission.

  Discussion:  Council thanked the outgoing commissioners for their service and offered well
  wishes.

PRESENTATION

3.  STATE OF THE CITY ADDRESS – F2M24-16

  Mayor Maza provided insight on the current state of the City and the progress made over the
  past year. The presentation is on file in the City Clerk’s office.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council received and filed the informational report.

PUBLIC HEARING

4.  PROPOSED ADJUSTMENTS IN VARIOUS CITY FEES AND SERVICE CHARGES –
  F2M15-48, F2M24-39, N2M24-49, R2M24-13

  This was the time and place set by Notice No. N2M24-49 for the City Council to hold a public
  hearing to consider adjusting various city fees and service charges. Director of Finance LIEU
  delivered a staff report. Resolution No. R2M16-4, previously adopted by the City Council, set
  forth the City’s Comprehensive Fee and Service Charge Schedule. The City maintained its
  fee schedule without increases since 2016. To ensure the sustainability of services, a
  Comprehensive Fee and Rate Study was conducted in 2023 to assist the City in determining
  appropriate fee levels for the various services provided by the City.

  While the update of the Comprehensive Fee and Service Charge Schedule would provide a
  fiscal impact in the form of additional revenue, it was pertinent to note the revenue was not
  intended to fund new services; rather the revenue was intended to offset the costs of providing
  existing services that are recoverable from fees. Considering the duration since the last fee
  increase, staff recommended a phased approach for certain fee increase over a three-year
  period, while others are recommended for full cost recovery. Staff recommended adoption of
  the new fees, as set forth in the staff report and exhibits to the attached Resolution.
  2
4-22-24
   Eric JOHNSON, President of Revenue and Cost Specialist, delivered an overview report on
  how to determine the full cost recovery fees. Ms. LIEU noted corrections on Exhibit A.

  Open Public Hearing: Mayor MAZA opened the public hearing.

  Public Comment:  Lewis McCAMMON, 105 N. Cordova St., distributed a handout and
  offered several corrections and suggestions to the Fee Schedule with regards to golf course
  fees. He went on to discussed the using land from the golf course for housing.

  Close Public Hearing: After receiving public comment, Mayor MAZA closed the public
  hearing.

  Discussion: Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER and Ms. LIEU briefly discussed
  business license fees for street food vendors. Councilmember LEE, Ms. LIEU, Ms. YU, and
  City Manager BINNQUIST discussed the contracted company to process parking citations,
  the hearing officer, and City staff. Ms. LEE continued to discuss ADU permit fees with
  Community Development Director HO. Ms. LEE requested staff provide a comparison survey
  of fees charged by other cities. Councilmember MALONEY supported the changes made. Vice
  Mayor PÉREZ also discussed business license fees and the application process for street
  food vendors with Ms. LIEU and Ms. YU. Ms. PÉREZ also requested the comparison fee study
  with other cities and discussed the recovery study conducted by the consultant as well as the
  informal comparison study conduced by City staff. Ms. PÉREZ and Mr. HO discussed changes
  in costs to appeal to Planning Commission versus costs to appeal to City Council. Ms. PÉREZ
  requested a more gradual increase to the fees associated with appeals to the Planning
  Commission. Mr. MAZA supported the gradual fee increases.

  Action Taken:  City Council adopted Resolution No. R2M24-39 entitled: A Resolution
  of the Alhambra City Council Modifying Resolution No. R2M16-4 Approving Various City Fees
  and Service Charges.

  Vote:  Moved:  LEE  Seconded:  PÉREZ
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, LEE, MALONEY, PÉREZ, MAZA
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

CONSENT AGENDA (Item Nos. 5 – 20)

All items listed under the Consent Agenda, with the exception of Item No. 17, were considered by the
City Council to be routine were enacted by one motion.

5.  NOTICE INVITING BIDS: SURFACE AND EXTERIOR CONCRETE REPAIRS FOR THE
  LIBRARY, POLICE DEPARTMENT AND CITY HALL BUILDINGS – F2M24-40, N2M24-50

  In August 2021, a facility assessment determined that the Library’s garage and basement
  levels haD cracking, and thus were in need of epoxy concrete repair and the removal of
  efflorescence. The recent rainstorms, made it apparent repairs should not be delayed, since
  seepage and water intrusion were experienced on both parking levels. Exterior cracking and
  water intrusion were also observed at the Police Department and City Hall buildings. During
  rainstorm events, seepage, water intrusion and flooding in the basements have been a
  frequent occurrence. City staff did not possess the expertise to complete this type of repair, as
  such staff requested the City Council authorize a Notice Inviting Bids that would include repairs
  to the Library, Police Department, and City Hall buildings.

  3
4-22-24
   Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council authorized staff to circulate a Notice Inviting Bids for
  Surface and Exterior Concrete Repairs to the Library, Police Department and City Hall
  buildings; and, directed staff to undertake the necessary steps to finalize Council’s action.

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded:  ANDRADE-STADLER
  Ayes:  PÉREZ, MALONEY, LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER, MAZA
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

6.  APPROVAL OF CHANGE ORDER TO CONTRACT FOR DESIGN SERVICES FOR ACTIVE
  TRANSPORTATION PROGRAM (ATP) CROSSWALK TRAFFIC CONTROL DEVICES
  PROJECT – F2M22-56, C2M23-6, M2M24-59

  On March 13, 2023, the City Council awarded a contract to Stantec Consulting Services, Inc.
  in the amount of $94,796.00 for the Design Services for the ATP Crosswalk Traffic Control
  Devices Project. During the design, it was determined that additional work was required to
  meet current standards. Additional work included traffic counts, incorporation of the Green
  Streets project components, and additional ADA curb ramps. The additional work required
  design services in the amount of $11,752.00. All other provisions of the contract would remain
  unchanged.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council approved a Change Order, subject to final language
  approval by the City Manager and City Attorney, in the amount of $11,752.00 for the
  Professional Engineering Design Services for the ATP Crosswalk Traffic Control Devices
  Project that was awarded to Stantec Consulting Services, Inc. (C2M23-6); and, directed staff
  to undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M24-59)

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded:  ANDRADE-STADLER
  Ayes:  PÉREZ, MALONEY, LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER, MAZA
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

7.  ACCEPTANCE OF A GRANT FROM THE CALIFORNIA EXTENDED WATER AND
  WASTEWATER ARREARAGE PAYMENT PROGRAM THROUGH FUNDING FROM THE
  STATE WATER RESOURCES CONTROL BOARD – F2M24-18, M2M24-60

  On November 30, 2023, staff applied to the California Extended Water and Wastewater
  Arrearage Payment Program (Program). The Program was developed to provide additional
  assistance to water and sewer systems that accrued residential and commercial customer
  arrearages during the COVID-19 pandemic from June 16, 2021 to December 31, 2022. The
  City received a payment of $98,360.46, the estimate staff requested in the Program
  application. The City previously received funding from the program in the amount of
  $278,640.59 for the relief period of March 4, 2020 through June 15, 2021. Once approved,
  staff would credit all eligible delinquent water and sewer accounts during the eligible period
  and notify each account holder of the amount credited to their account, per the grant
  guidelines. Customers would not have to repay any payments received.

  Discussion:  None.

  4
4-22-24
   Action Taken:  City Council accepted a grant from the California Extended Water and
  Wastewater Arrearage Payment Program through funding from the State Water Resources
  Control Board in the amount of $98,360.46 to pay delinquent water and sewer bills; directed
  the Finance Director to increase revenue account 404.00.42808 and expense account
  404.80.8681.68087 by $98,360.46; and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to
  finalize Council’s action. (M2M24-60)

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded:  ANDRADE-STADLER
  Ayes:  PÉREZ, MALONEY, LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER, MAZA
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

8.  NOTICE OF COMPLETION: FRONT STREET WATER MAIN REPLACEMENT AND ZONE
  CHANGE - PHASE 1 – F2M19-20, C2M23-72, M2M24-64

  On August 28, 2023, the City Council awarded Contract C2M23-72 to Teichert Energy &
  Utilities Group, Inc for the Front Street Water Main Replacement and Zone Change - Phase 1
  Project in the amount of $908,785.00. There were two authorized change orders during the
  project. The change orders were to relocate a utility vault, replace irrigation services to the
  median, additional paving and also included various miscellaneous items credited to City. The
  change order increased the total amount of the contract by $65,062.83, for a total project cost
  of $973,847.83. The project was completed in accordance with the City’s requirements and
  specifications. As such, it would be appropriate for the City Council to accept the project as
  complete and instruct the City Clerk that the Notice of Completion be filed with the County of
  Los Angeles Recorder’s Office.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council accepted the work of Teichert Energy & Utilities Group,
  Inc. for the Front Street Water Main Replacement and Zone Change - Phase 1 Project as
  complete in the amount of $973,847.83; directed the City Clerk to file a Notice of Completion
  with the County of Los Angeles for recordation; released the five percent retention 35 days
  from the date of recordation if no liens are filed; and, directed staff to undertake the steps
  necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M24-64)

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded:  ANDRADE-STADLER
  Ayes:  PÉREZ, MALONEY, LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER, MAZA
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

9.  ACCEPTANCE OF GRANT FROM CALRECYCLE UNDER THE SB 1383 LOCAL
  ASSISTANCE GRANT PROGRAM – F2M23-18, M2M24-61

  On October 23, 2023, the City Council approved Resolution No. R2M23-52 for the submittal
  of a grant application to the CalRecycle SB 1383 Local Assistance Grant Program. The City
  submitted an application for $152,477 in funding to expand marketing efforts on organics
  recycling, purchase of recycling and organic waste receptacles, and to procure commercial-
  grade equipment for the application of compost and mulch on City facilities. On February 26,
  2024, CalRecycle notified that the City was selected to receive a grant award in the amount of
  $218,610.

  Discussion:  None.

  5
4-22-24
   Action Taken:  City Council accepted a grant in the amount of $218,610 from the
  Department of Resources Recycling and Recovery (CalRecycle) under the SB 1383 Local
  Assistance Grant Program; appropriated revenue and expenditure funds; authorized the City
  Manager, or designee, to execute all documents related to grant implementation; and, directed
  staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M24-61)

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded:  ANDRADE-STADLER
  Ayes:  PÉREZ, MALONEY, LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER, MAZA
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

10.  ACCEPTANCE OF FY 2023 URBAN AREA SECURITY INITIATIVE GRANT AND
  APPROPRIATION OF GRANT REVENUES AND EXPENDITURES – F2M1-106, C2M24-22,
  M2M24-62

  As a designated Core City, the City of Los Angeles is eligible for additional funding through
  the Urban Area Strategic Security Initiative (UASI) Grant Program that is administered by the
  Department of Homeland Security. In addition to the Core City, individual cities that are
  contiguous to the City of Los Angeles are also eligible for funding. The Police and Fire
  Departments jointly submitted a grant request for $452,298.00 to the Approval Authority who
  administers the UASI Grant Program and the request was approved for $146,818.00 allocated
  to the Police Department and $305,480.00 allocated to the Fire Department. Funding would
  be used to purchase software licensing for the Police Department’s Automated License Plate
  Reader (ALPR) program and for the purchase of an armored police rescue vehicle for shared
  use by Alhambra, South Pasadena and Monterey Park. The funds awarded to the Fire
  Department would be used for Urban Search and Rescue equipment and training as well as
  for sustainment and maintenance of the Alhambra Fire Training Facility.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  Accept the 2023 Urban Area Strategic Security Initiative Grant (UASI)
  in the amount of $452,298.00; directed the Finance Director to amend the City’s 2023-2024
  Adopted Budget by increasing the Police Department revenue by $146,818.00 in account
  101.20.42399 and appropriating $146,818 in account 101.20.2010.99399 and increasing the
  Fire Department revenue by $305,480.00 in account 101.30.42399 and appropriating
  $305,480.00 in account 101.30.3610.99399; and, directed staff to undertake the steps
  necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M24-62)

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded:  ANDRADE-STADLER
  Ayes:  PÉREZ, MALONEY, LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER, MAZA
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

11.  AWARD CONTRACT: GRANTS MANAGEMENT SOFTWARE – F2M24-41, C2M24-24,
  M2M24-63

  Under the City’s 2021-22 Strategic Plan, the City Council emphasized securing grant funding
  for a variety of projects, needs, and interests of the City. Staff requested an investment in a
  grant management system to facilitate the centralization of grant information; to monitor
  compliance including reporting and project progress; and to ease the search for new grant
  opportunities, particularly in relation to grants that align with the City’s strategic priorities. There
  were several public agencies currently utilizing eCivis to help manage their grants portfolio.
  The product is a fully integrated cloud-based system that propels the grants management
  6
4-22-24
   lifecycle. City Departments could login the system to help research and maintain the City’s
  grant information. Staff sought to procure the grants software system via cooperative
  purchase, allowable under Alhambra Municipal Code Section 3.36.080(B)(3). Carahsoft
  Technology Corporation offers products and services from eCivis under GSA Contract No.
  47QSWA18D008F. The contract period for the GSA contract is from August 2018 through
  August 2028; therefore, the City could piggyback for this grant management system under
  this procurement.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council awarded a contract, subject to final language approval by
  the City Manager and City Attorney, to eCivis Inc. for the implementation and subscription of
  grants management software, in the amount of $32,775 for one year with four one-year
  extensions through April 2029; authorized the City Manager to execute the contract and annual
  extensions pursuant to satisfactory performance; and, directed staff to undertake the steps
  necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M24-63)

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded:  ANDRADE-STADLER
  Ayes:  PÉREZ, MALONEY, LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER, MAZA
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

12.  RESOLUTION DELEGATING AUTHORITY TO SUBMIT EMPLOYER ORIGINATED
  DISABILITY APPLICATIONS TO THE CALIFORNIA PUBLIC EMPLOYEES’ RETIREMENT
  SYSTEM – F2M24-2, R2M24-12

  An application for a CalPERS disability or industrial disability retirement may be initiated by an
  employee or an employer. In the past, CalPERS accepted Employer Originated Applications
  submitted by City staff. However, CalPERS recently notified the City that in order to maintain
  the status quo and accept Employer Originated Disability Applications, the City Council must
  first officially delegate authority to staff via a resolution, per Government Code Section 21152.
  Therefore, staff requested that the City Council adopt a resolution delegating authority to the
  City Manager and Director of Human Resources & Risk Management to submit Employer
  Originated Disability Applications.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council adopted Resolution No. R2M24-12 entitled: A Resolution
  of the Alhambra City Council delegating authority to submit Employer Originated Disability
  Applications to CALPERS

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded:  ANDRADE-STADLER
  Ayes:  PÉREZ, MALONEY, LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER, MAZA
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

13.  AUTHORIZE RFP: PROFESSIONAL CONSULTING SERVICES TO PREPARE OBJECTIVE
  DESIGN STANDARDS AND DESIGN GUIDELINES – F2M24-42, RFP2M24-10

  The City Council’s 2024 Strategic Plan identified the creation of design guidelines for multi-
  family dwellings, as well as commercial and mixed-use buildings, as one objective of the
  overarching goal of improving housing opportunities in the City. To achieve this Strategic Plan
  objective, Staff sought to solicit proposals for professional consulting services to assist with
  7
4-22-24
   the preparation of citywide objective design standards and design guidelines. The RFP
  identified the scope and services required for this endeavor with details provided on the
  expectations of the consultant, including a recommendation for appropriate community
  outreach and if necessary, phasing of the project. The primary focus of the project was to have
  the appropriate standards and guidelines in place that would foster greater architectural
  compatibility throughout the City and the cultivation of neighborhood identities through design.
  The project deliverables would be used to enhance and supplement the objective design
  standards in the City’s Zoning Ordinance.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council authorized the distribution of a Request for Proposals for
  professional consulting services to assist in the preparation of citywide design standards and
  design guidelines.

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded:  ANDRADE-STADLER
  Ayes:  PÉREZ, MALONEY, LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER, MAZA
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

14.  AWARD CONTRACT: ECONOMIC AND MARKET ANALYSIS CONSULTING SERVICES –
  F2M24-20, RFP2M24-1, C2M24-25, M2M24-65

  On January 8, 2024, the City Council authorized the distribution of a Request for Proposals
  (RFP) to prospective firms and consultants to conduct economic and market analysis services
  for the Economic Development Action Plan. The City received nine proposals. Staff evaluated
  all proposals, interviewed three proposers and selected ECONorthwest as the most qualified
  consultant. Staff reviewed and evaluated the proposals based on the RFP requirements, which
  included understanding of the project scope, approach and methodology, experience with
  economic development and project cost.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council awarded a contract, subject to final language approval by
  the City Manager and City Attorney, to ECONorthwest for economic and market analysis
  consulting services in an amount not to exceed $75,000 over two years; and, directed staff to
  undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M24-65)

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded:  ANDRADE-STADLER
  Ayes:  PÉREZ, MALONEY, LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER, MAZA
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

15.  AWARD CONTRACT: PROFESSIONAL CONSULTING SERVICES TO DEVELOP THE
  LOCAL HAZARD MITIGATION PLAN - F2M23-70, RFP2M23-25, C2M24-26, M2M24-66

  On October 9, 2023 the City Council accepted the grant for a Hazard Mitigation Assistance
  grant in the amount of $135,450, with a match commitment of $15,050 from the Hazard
  Mitigation Grant Program funded by FEMA and the State of California Governor’s Office of
  Emergency Services through subawards. On October 23, 2023 the City Council approved the
  distribution of a Request for Proposals RFP2M23-25 for professional consulting services to
  develop the LHMP. A total of six proposals were accepted by the due date of February 6, 2024.
  Staff reviewed and evaluated the proposals based on the requirements of the RFP, which
  8
4-22-24
   included Responsiveness to RFP, Experience and Knowledge of Entity and Personnel, Project
  Approach, and Costs. Black & Veatch Corporation was selected because it best suited the
  City’s needs.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council awarded a contract, subject to final language approval by
  the City Manager and City Attorney, in the amount not to exceed $144,920.00 for the
  development of a new Local Hazard Mitigation Plan (LHMP); and directed staff to undertake
  the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M24-66)

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded:  ANDRADE-STADLER
  Ayes:  PÉREZ, MALONEY, LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER, MAZA
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

16.  AWARD CONTRACT: FIRE PREVENTION COMPLIANCE SOFTWARE AND REPORTING
  SERVICES – F2M24-43, C2M24-27, M2M24-67

  Community Risk Reduction (CRR) is a division of the Alhambra Fire Department (AFD). CRR
  staff is dedicated to increasing safety, preventing, or reducing fire losses and ensuring
  compliance with applicable codes and ordinances. The communication and delivery of reports
  from third parties has been done manually and has not allowed for efficient tracking,
  processing and enforcement of the codes. Brycer was designed to consolidate efforts into a
  single operation to streamline the reporting process. Brycer utilized TCE software that would
  track and drive fire code compliance and help reduce false alarm activity through a simple
  web-based service that would allow the CRR to connect to contractors who inspect, test, and
  maintain fire protection systems. Inspectors could then efficiently review reports, track
  deficiencies, notify parties and ensure compliance of fire and life safety systems. Brycer would
  provide a database of the buildings in our jurisdiction and helps to achieve greater fire
  protection systems reliability at zero cost. TCE would allow for service providers to submit
  copies of their inspection and testing reports to AFD electronically, facilitating a more efficient
  review, tracking and follow-up process with occupants to correct deficiencies and maintain
  systems. The term of the proposed Brycer Agreement would be for three years, effective June
  1, 2024, and would be renewed on June 1, 2027 for two terms of one year each pursuant to
  satisfactory performance. Per the Alhambra Municipal Code (Section 3.38.050), the contract
  procedures may be dispensed when the services can only be obtained from one source (sole
  source). In this case, the reporting support services were exclusively available through Brycer.
  The reporting services of Brycer were highly specialized and essential to the City’s CRR
  operations.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council approved a contract with Brycer, LLC, subject to final
  language approval by the City Manager and City Attorney, to implement The Compliance
  Engine (TCE) for fire code compliance and reporting services for a three-year period with an
  option for two one-year contract extensions, and authorized the City Manager to execute the
  extensions if the services are satisfactory; authorized the City Manager or designee to execute
  the necessary documents; and directed staff to undertake the necessary steps to finalize
  Council’s action. (M2M24-67)

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded:  ANDRADE-STADLER
  Ayes:  PÉREZ, MALONEY, LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER, MAZA
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council approved as submitted Final Check List (247440 thru

 20.  NOVEMBER 5, 2024 ALHAMBRA GENERAL MUNICIPAL ELECTION: ADOPTION OF AN
  ORDINANCE CALLING THE ELECTION AND OF A RESOLUTION REGARDING
  CONSOLIDATION WITH THE STATEWIDE GENERAL ELECTION TO BE HELD THAT
  SAME DATE IN LOS ANGELES COUNTY – F2M24-38, O2M24-4829, R2M24-14

  On April 8, 2024, the City Council introduced for first reading Ordinance No. O2M22-4802
  providing for a General Municipal Election to be held on November 5, 2024 for the purpose of
  submitting to the qualified voters the following named officers: Councilperson of the Third
  District, full term; and, Councilperson of the Fourth District, full term. Pursuant to the Alhambra
  Charter as recently amended by Measure V in 2020, these offices shall be nominated from
  and elected by districts. The Alhambra City Charter provides that General Municipal Elections
  shall be consolidated with the Statewide General Elections to be held on the first Tuesday
  following the first Monday of every even-numbered year; hence, the next General Municipal
  Election for the City of Alhambra, would be held on Tuesday, November 5, 2024. The City of
  Alhambra historically has consolidated its General Municipal Elections with those held on the
  same date in the County of Los Angeles. Based on economies of scale, such consolidation
  has resulted in considerable cost savings for the City. Therefore, staff requested that the City
  Council adopt the ordinance calling the November 5, 2024 General Municipal Election as well
  as a resolution regarding consolidation with the Statewide General Election to be held that
  same day in Los Angeles County.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council, by one motion, took the following actions:

  1.  Declared introduced for its second reading and adopt the following ordinance entitled:

  Ordinance No. O2M24-4829: An Ordinance of the Alhambra City Council providing
  for a General Municipal Election in said city to be held on November 5, 2024 and
  providing for the consolidation of the General Municipal Election with the Statewide
  General Election, said election being held for the election of the following city officials,
  to wit: Councilperson of the Third District, full term; and, Councilperson of the Fourth
  District, full term; and,

  2.  Adopted Resolution No. R2M24-14 entitled: A Resolution of the Alhambra City
  Council requesting the Board of Supervisors of the County of Los Angeles to order the
  consolidation of an Alhambra General Municipal Election to be held on November 5,
  2024 with the Statewide General Election to be held in Los Angeles County the same
  day, to authorize the Board of Supervisors of the County of Los Angeles to canvass
  the returns of said General Municipal Election and to request that the Registrar of
  Voters of said County be permitted to render specified services to the City of Alhambra
  relating to the conduct of said General Municipal Election pursuant to Elections Code
  Section 10403
